title: Dynamic Quantization Orchestrator + Runtime Calibration Harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a runtime component that dynamically selects among FP16/FP8/INT8 execution paths using per-model quantization profiles and a lightweight on-node calibration harness. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by exploiting lower-precision kernels where safe, while ensuring accuracy regressions are detected and mitigated automatically.
background: We have several model families with validated quantization profiles (FP8, INT8) produced by the calibration pipeline, but current dispatch is static per-deployment. This ticket bundles a runtime orchestrator that: 1) evaluates per-request suitability for lower-precision kernels using cached statistics and short calibration probes; 2) chooses kernel implementation at layer-granularity when beneficial; 3) falls back to higher precision when accuracy risk or latency SLO violations are detected.
proposed_design:
- Maintain a per-model QuantProfile object (metadata only) that includes per-layer quant modes, recommended kernel variants, and calibrated scale/error stats.
- Instrument a lightweight probe request path: for new model variants or after config changes, run small-batch calibration probes against a compact calibration set cached at the node.
- At dispatch time, consult runtime heuristics combining: recent probe accuracy deltas, sequence-length bucket, client latency budget, and current GPU load.
- Use a scoring function to choose either 'safe' (FP16 fallback), 'aggressive' (FP8/INT8 layers applied), or 'probe' (allow experimental lower precision for small fraction).
- Implement a fast path in the kernel router: path key = model_id + quant_profile_id + seq_bucket + load_bucket. Cache compiled kernels per path.
calibration_workflow:
- Upstream: CI produces quant profiles via calibration pipeline with per-layer stats and a 1k-example validation shard.
- Node-level: store a compact (100-example) calibration shard for fast probes.
- Probe flow: run on model variant activation and when profile changes. Measure delta on representative metrics (logit-EMB cosine, top-k agreement).
- If delta < threshold, mark profile as 'eligible' for aggressive dispatch; else mark 'restricted'.
- Periodic re-probing schedule configurable per-model (default 24h or after 500k tokens).
validation_plan:
- Define an evaluation harness that runs the compact calibration shard and a held-out accuracy set (5k examples) across precision paths.
- Acceptance thresholds: overall utility metric drop <= 0.5% and task-specific pass-rates within historical variance.
- Monitor production: shadow mode for 2 weeks with telemetry comparing FP16 vs chosen mixed-precision outputs (agreement rate, per-token divergence, latency, and token cost).
- Rollback criteria: agreement < 98.5% on critical prompt buckets or 99th percentile latency increase > 10%.
rollout_plan: 1) Dev: unit tests + simulated probes on CI; 2) Canary: enable orchestrator in one region for internal customers, shadow mixed-precision decisions; 3) Gradual rollout: 10% traffic with canary heuristics for 48h, then 50% for 7 days; 4) Full: flip on by default for models passing probes and shadow validation.
engineering_tasks: API: expose QuantProfile (read-only) in model catalog
Runtime: implement path scoring and kernel router integration
Storage: node-local compact calibration shard persistence
CI: add calibration probe integration tests
Monitoring: dashboards for agreement rates and probe outcomes
Docs: operational runbook for probe failures and rollbacks
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Tradeoff: aggressive per-layer FP8 can provide cost savings but increases regression risk. We favor conservative defaults with opt-in aggressive profiles.
- Decision: keep quant profiles immutable for a deployed variant; changes must version the variant to avoid silent behavior changes.
- Tradeoff: probe frequency vs cost. Default 24h balances staleness and probe overhead; customers can opt-in to more aggressive schedules.
risks: undetected accuracy regressions for rare prompt-types
complexity in kernel cache invalidation causing memory pressure
edge cases where mixed-precision interacts with fused kernels leading to numerical instability
mitigations: shadow mode for 2 weeks before enabling path decisions
per-customer opt-out and explicit platform flagging
automatic fallback to FP16 on any probe failure or anomaly
limit aggressive dispatch to layers marked as 'quant-safe' by calibration pipeline
open_questions: What is the acceptable probe budget per node in sustained load?
Should customers be able to provide their own calibration shards? If so, how to secure them?
Do we need per-tenant tailoring of scoring thresholds?
